name: Afrikaner nationalism
summary: Afrikaner nationalism is an ethnic nationalism that holds Afrikaners to be a distinct, God-placed nation with its own language (Afrikaans), Calvinist faith and fatherland. Its aim was an Afrikaner-led republic free of British influence, which in power from 1948 meant apartheid and separate development, Christian National Education and legislated Puritanism. After 1994 it survives mainly as demands for cultural protection and self-determination, such as a volkstaat or Orania.
scope: The mainstream of the movement at its peak, from the National Party and Broederbond (1920s) through Hertzog, Malan and Verwoerd to the 1961 republic and the 1948-1994 apartheid state. Based on Verwoerd's 1959 Senate speech, and the scholarly and encyclopedic accounts cited. Later volkstaat, Orania and Freedom Front Plus positions and the far-right AWB are noted but not the profile's basis.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Volkskapitalisme stressed Afrikaner enterprise and self-help; state health provision is not documented as a goal, though apartheid-era welfare for whites existed, so inferred mild opposition to universal guarantees.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Nationalist economics served white Afrikaner workers and employers via job reservation rather than wage floors; inferred from the economic programme in the sources.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Volkskapitalisme sought to steer the economy toward Afrikaner ownership through Afrikaner-run institutions rather than trusting an anonymous market seen as British or Jewish.

public-ownership.rationale: Afrikaner nationalists created state enterprises and also Afrikaner private capital; the sources show both, so adherents split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Volkskapitalisme aimed to build Afrikaner capital, so heavy wealth taxes cut against the project; inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Nationalists backed white-only, nation-oriented unions and opposed class-based labour politics such as the 1922 Rand Revolt; general union enthusiasm is not documented.

property-fundamental.rationale: Verwoerd defended white control of land and states, and Afrikaner capital building presupposes property; inferred, though the volk's claims could override individual title.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Nationalists wanted state steering of an economy seen as foreign-run but also promoted Afrikaner corporations such as Sanlam; no clear line.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not documented; the movement was concerned with the poor-white question yet wary of state dependence, so adherents split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Class-based ownership schemes contradict a nationalism that opposed class politics and socialism; inferred from anti-communism and volkskapitalisme.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The apartheid state treated security as paramount against internal enemies (communism, black resistance); inferred support for surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Nationalists legislated Calvinist Puritanism (banning pornography and gambling); drug legalisation would fit poorly.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not an issue the movement addressed in those terms; it used censorship for moral and security ends but defended its own speech, so mild opposition inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Hertzog and Verwoerd were strong leaders and some nationalists admired Nazi-style states, but the republic worked through parliament; adherents split.

state-harmful.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism sought its own state and used it to enforce apartheid; the idea that the state is harmful is foreign to it.

limit-guns.rationale: Boer commando tradition and white security concerns make strict gun control unattractive; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: The apartheid state expanded police and military under Verwoerd and later governments, justified by white survival against a black majority and communism.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Legislated Puritanism under the National Party criminalised adultery and banned pornography; sex work would be opposed.

decide-locally.rationale: The movement valued ethnic self-determination (volkstaat, homelands) but ran a centralised state; split between devolution and central control.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not documented; the apartheid state's law-and-order stress suggests a punitive tilt.

traditional-family.rationale: Afrikaner Calvinism and legislated Puritanism treated the Christian family as the basis of the volk.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Dutch Reformed Calvinist moral order and enforced Puritanism leave no room for it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Calvinist moral order and the National Party's legislated morality imply strong opposition.

more-religion-public.rationale: Christian-national doctrine made Calvinism part of public life, schools and state.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Adherents defended separate development as just and rejected redress; the project ran the other direction.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Calvinist traditional views on sexes imply rejection; not directly documented.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defence of Afrikaans, history and Calvinist identity is the core of the ideology.

gradual-change.rationale: Nationalists were radical in building a republic and apartheid yet defended the established order against change after 1948; split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Verwoerd led academics petitioning against admitting Jewish refugees in 1936, showing hostility to immigration that dilutes the volk, though white immigration was later promoted.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Afrikaner nationalists resisted British imperial ties and later the UN; Verwoerd left the Commonwealth in 1961 rather than accept outside criticism.

free-trade.rationale: Verwoerd's Die Transvaler combined republicanism with protectionism, and volkskapitalisme was nationalist in aim.

nation-first.rationale: The 1915 slogan 'South Africa first' and the republic ideal put Afrikaner/national interest ahead of imperial or global ties.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not documented; non-interference and rejection of outside moral claims suggests opposition.

open-borders.rationale: The project was a bounded volk and separate states; open borders contradict it.

limit-growth.rationale: Not an issue for the ideology; development of the nation's economy was valued.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; no position in sources, inferred from economic nationalism.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The sources show no stance on technology as a cure-all; Calvinist providence, not progress, frames Afrikaner history, so adherents are split.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The apartheid state developed nuclear capability and energy self-sufficiency; inferred, anachronistic for the ideology itself.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nationalists staged the 1914 Maritz rebellion and some later AWB militancy, but mainstream held to constitutional means; split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Not documented; volk-based politics emphasised the people, though the Broederbond elite guided it.

central-planning.rationale: Volkskapitalisme was capitalist in form; Afrikaner nationalists opposed communism.

socialized-markets.rationale: Anti-communist, pro-Afrikaner-capital; public or worker-owned market schemes not on the agenda.

land-value-tax.rationale: No Afrikaner nationalist source discusses land taxation, and farmers' ownership was central to the volk, so no position can be inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: Afrikaner capital accumulation across generations is part of volkskapitalisme.

basic-income.rationale: Not documented; unconditional transfers sit poorly with Calvinist work ethic.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Verwoerd's editorials combined republicanism, populism and protectionism, and the National Party built state industry behind tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Nationalists used state corporations and Afrikaner financial institutions to direct capital toward Afrikaner advancement.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Poor-white farmer ideal was present historically but not a stated principle in these sources.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Communism was a defined enemy; abolishing wages is alien.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not documented; no hint of monetary radicalism.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Broederbond-style organic Afrikaner institutions have corporatist flavour, but state-recognised wage bargaining is not documented.

one-party-rule.rationale: The National Party dominated 1948 to 1994 and the Broederbond ran the state, but multi-party white elections continued and rival right parties existed.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Republicanism was the movement's ideal against British Crown ties; the 1961 republic was its culmination.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents valued democracy for the white volk only; Verwoerd argued numbers decide power and so opposed majority democracy in the whole country.

direct-votes.rationale: The 1960 republic referendum used a direct vote but the system was representative; no support for direct lawmaking is documented.

workers-councils.rationale: Opposed to socialist ideas; class councils contradict volk unity.

right-to-secede.rationale: Afrikaner self-determination includes volkstaat and Cape independence ideas, and the Boer republics seceded from British control; inferred for adherents' own group.

natural-rulers.rationale: Du Toit argued Afrikaners were destined to rule, and apartheid assumed white guardianship over other groups.

political-violence-never.rationale: Boer rebellions and AWB militancy show violence accepted by some; mainstream justified state force.

war-builds-character.rationale: Boer War memory is sacred history, but no doctrine that war builds character; split.

separate-church-state.rationale: Christian-national ideology fused Calvinism and state; the Dutch Reformed Church backed segregation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Laws were expected to follow Christian-national principles and Calvinist morals, though not a theocratic code.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The movement wanted a strong state for the volk, with its own army, navy and police as Verwoerd said.

military-superiority.rationale: Verwoerd advocated a white state that controls its own army, navy and police; regional military strength was a security priority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism is ethnic nationalism, with a volk and fatherland.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The ideology saw nations, not classes, as the unit and opposed class politics.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism built a racial hierarchy under apartheid and never discussed equality of outcome as such; rejection is inferred from segregation policy.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Verwoerd defended Bantu homelands as national units, and later nationalists petitioned the UN for Afrikaner indigenous status; applied to own group chiefly.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The movement's identity was anti-British but it rejected redress for colonised peoples and denied being colonial itself.

civilizational-union.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism was parochial, with kinship to Dutch but no union scheme documented.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Calvinist duty to the volk emphasised communal duty over self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Volk-centred and Calvinist ethic subordinates individual claims to the nation; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The sources are silent on environmental philosophy; Calvinist stewardship and farming heritage point both ways, leaving it neutral.

limit-population.rationale: Not documented; but Verwoerd feared black numerical majority, which implies preference for white numbers rather than limits for whites; mildly negative.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Nationalists pursued industrial advancement for Afrikaners; anachronistic.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Conservatism about institutions and morals; not documented.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Security-state mindset implies state access; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Nationalism looked back to Trek and republics yet built a modern state; split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Volk ideology and Calvinist principle came first in policy; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Mainstream nationalism worked through party, Broederbond and parliament.

means-match-ends.rationale: The movement's methods ranged from parliamentary politics to secret networks and rebellion, and no principle linking means to ends is documented.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communist principle rejected by anti-communist nationalists.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialist principle opposed; volkskapitalisme pursued capital accumulation.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist claim rejected; Afrikaner business was promoted.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Anti-communism is a documented root of the ideology.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation is communist; Afrikaner nationalism rooted in farmers' ownership.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not documented; the state was valued as the volk's instrument.

harm-principle.rationale: Legislated Puritanism restricted private morality beyond harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The volk as a group with rights to self-determination is central, and Verwoerd's policy treated rights by group.

conscription.rationale: The apartheid state conscripted white men; defence of the volk justified it.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not documented; belonging to the volk and rooted in a fatherland suggests opposition.

state-as-business.rationale: The state expresses the volk, not a business; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not documented; freedom meant national self-rule rather than material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Nationalists saw English press as hostile and built their own Afrikaans media; not a stated thesis about power over elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Verwoerd's 1927 memo denied innate mental differences, while others like Cronje grounded segregation in difference of culture; adherents split.

organic-representation.rationale: The Broederbond and Afrikaner cultural bodies show organic institutions, though parliament ran via parties.

total-state.rationale: Some interwar nationalists admired Nazi-style states but mainstream apartheid state did not direct every area; mixed.

national-rebirth.rationale: Du Toit's and Broederbond rhetoric of awakening after the Boer War defeat; but no 'decadence' doctrine.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Verwoerd defended a limited white state and homelands, not expansion; the Boer republics sought their own territory.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The republic relied on constitutional office and party, not personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Apartheid pass laws and labour control tied black labour; statement is about legal bonding to a lord, which was not doctrine.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Christian National Education held that schooling should rest on Calvinist and national foundations, implying knowledge is not neutral.

universal-morality.rationale: Calvinist belief in God's law implies universal moral truths, though knowable by revelation rather than reason.

single-common-good.rationale: Volk unity is the common good for the nation, yet the movement was explicitly sectional.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not documented; some Afrikaner nationalists were antisemitic, though the NP later allied with Israel; split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not documented; citizenship questions in the movement were about white settlers and the volk.

revive-national-language.rationale: Afrikaans was raised from a spoken Dutch variety to an official language in 1925, which is elevation rather than revival of a disused tongue; the statement fits only loosely, so mild agreement is inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Christian National Education favoured mother-tongue schools with religious instruction, but the state ran them; no voucher stance.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: No source records the movement's fiscal doctrine; the NP state ran state corporations without a documented stance on deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: The movement valued economic empowerment of Afrikaners over economic freedom as doctrine.

rule-by-example.rationale: Nationalists relied on law and strong enforcement.

national-self-determination.rationale: Diederichs held nations have a God-given right to exist separately; Afrikaner self-determination is the core claim.

force-without-un.rationale: Anti-UN stance and Namibia/Angola policies imply willingness; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Afrikaner Calvinism opposed the Enlightenment and liberalism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare targeted at whites in practice; citizens-only inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nationalism asserted volk unity across classes against class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving heritage and monuments such as Voortrekker Monument is central.

dominated-front.rationale: Afrikaners saw themselves as Western and Christian anti-communist, though opposed British influence.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalist unions sought to organise white workers by nation against international socialism, as after the Rand Revolt.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Calvinist and traditional view of men's and women's roles in the volk.

ban-interest.rationale: Volkskapitalisme relied on banks and insurers (Sanlam, Volkskas).

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Apartheid laws classified and separated races in residence, education and facilities.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The apartheid state produced coal oil (Sasol) for self-sufficiency; inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism was exclusive on ethnic grounds, so assimilation into Afrikaner culture was a question; white immigrants were encouraged to assimilate to white culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not a documented theme, though 'swart gevaar' fears of numerical majority existed.

proportional-representation.rationale: The NP won power under first-past-the-post in 1948; PR not favoured.

national-mission.rationale: Afrikaners saw themselves as a chosen people with Trek as Exodus, but a mission to spread its government to others was not doctrine.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Traditional gender order accepted, not criticised.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Populist strains criticised English-led elites but ruled themselves.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not documented; Calvinism leans against eugenic coercion.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: De Klerk-era ideology defended security forces; accountability sought mostly by opponents.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Strong interventionist state in economy and society.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Apartheid banned mixed marriages and sexual relations across racial lines.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Apartheid law classified people by race and denied Black South Africans equal rights before the law; Calvinist talk of worth before God did not translate into legal equality.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Adherents regarded themselves as an indigenous people of Africa and rejected the colonial label, petitioning the UN for indigenous status.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Group-based law and separate institutions fit the ideology better.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism was tied to one Calvinist church family but the sources document no push to restrict conversion by law.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Irrelevant to Afrikaner culture; cattle farming is central.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Christian National Education put Calvinist instruction in schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Socialist-state doctrine not applicable, though siege-mentality justified a strong state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Consent of the white volk mattered; Verwoerd denied majority consent in the whole country.

population-transfer.rationale: Homeland resettlement moved Black South Africans into ethnic reserves and stripped their representation.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not an adherent principle; state force defended apartheid.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The apartheid state banned the Communist Party and ANC in 1950s-60s; inferred for nationalists.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed, though freedom from British domination was core.

separated-powers.rationale: Parliamentary supremacy was a feature of the NP state; mixed.

vanguard-party.rationale: Communist concept rejected; though the Broederbond acted as an elite vanguard for the volk, the statement is about revolutionary class politics.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Poor-white upliftment was a nationalist concern; but not general priority to poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing sales were a later British policy debate with no equivalent in the sources, so no stance can be inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Nationalist state limited strikes, especially for Black workers; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The sources link poverty to the poor-white problem and economic exclusion rather than to population growth, and give no firm view.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Segregation and the ethnic nation rest on the view that mixed peoples cannot live in one polity; Verwoerd and Cronje reasoned this way.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The apartheid state used emergency powers and detention without trial against opponents; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price fixing in scarcity is not discussed in the sources on the movement's economics, so it is left neutral.

party-controls-media.rationale: The NP controlled the broadcaster and censored but Afrikaans press was independent-ish; split.

party-commands-army.rationale: The state, not party, commanded the SADF formally.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Protective of the volk against dilution; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not part of the movement's institutions.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: NP and Broederbond demanded discipline and expelled dissenters.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Afrikaner nationalists fought British imperial authority and took South Africa out of the Commonwealth in 1961, which clearly implies opposing supranational pooling, though EU-style unions postdate their peak.

head-commands-forces.rationale: State president was a ceremonial office in 1961 constitution; mixed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Reformed churches are governed by synods and consistories, not bishops.

clerical-rule.rationale: Dutch Reformed clergy influenced but did not rule; Calvinist spheres doctrine separates church and state authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Nationalists were intensely patriotic; they opposed WWI entry but sought to uphold South African/Afrikaner state.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The state banned pornography and censored works to protect Calvinist morals.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The 1961 republic had a ceremonial state president chosen by parliament, so presidential term limits were not a live issue for adherents.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall votes are not part of the movement's parliamentary tradition and none of the sources address them.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Opposition to being drawn into British wars (WWI, WWII) shows desire to avoid foreign commitments.

people-in-arms.rationale: Commando tradition supports armed citizenry, but the state kept a standing professional army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Afrikaner identity was rooted in the farm and Trek, though urbanisation was embraced; inferred.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Nationalism was intellectual in leadership (Broederbond professors), so split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Verwoerd stressed distinct races with different values; Cronje saw Afrikaner culture as needing protection; some said cultures differ only, others ranked.

death-penalty.rationale: The apartheid state used capital punishment extensively; Calvinist retributive tradition.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Calvinist morality and Christian National Education resist it.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Christian National Education insisted on Calvinist foundations; evolution was disfavoured.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The National Party banned pornography as part of legislated Puritanism.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The volk is defined by ancestry and language; citizenship laws in the apartheid state followed race.

minority-language-support.rationale: Afrikaners demanded Afrikaans-medium schooling against English dominance, yet the apartheid state imposed Afrikaans on Black pupils, which set off Soweto in 1976; support for minority languages in general is not shown.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Adherents defended their own Calvinist norms in state law; exemptions for minority faiths are not discussed in the sources.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conformity to the volk and Puritanism is valued.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Volkskapitalisme sought to take economic control from British and Jewish capital, arguing that political power was not enough.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1960 referendum and 1961 republic constitution passed by parliament; not stated.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The apartheid state restricted freedoms but justification was security, not growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Verwoerd resisted obligations to outsiders; not documented.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: South Africa built its own bombs under NP governments; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The 1961 republic had state president chosen by parliament; mild.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The sources mention Afrikaner banks and insurers but nothing on central bank independence, so no position can be inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territory is sacred to volk history; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Calvinist stewardship might support this while Verwoerd defended white ownership strongly, so adherents plausibly split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anti-communists would hold the USSR as enemy, not analyse it as state-capitalist.

collective-defense.rationale: The NP stressed independence and neutrality towards Commonwealth, but anti-communist alliance with the West; split.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not documented; South Africa held South West Africa itself.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church and nation were intertwined; the Dutch Reformed Church formally backed segregation.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The state president was ceremonial after 1961.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Republic opposed Black homeland secession yet claimed self-determination for Afrikaners; split.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not documented, though homelands were semi-autonomous under white control.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Republican and Calvinist; kings and divinity of rulers rejected.

flat-income-tax.rationale: No source addresses the shape of income tax; the question was not part of the movement's programme.

character-from-environment.rationale: Adherents attributed national character to history and culture, but not documented.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty yet constitutional republic; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is an anachronism that nothing in the movement's texts addresses; neutral.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The sources show a parliamentary republic with white-only franchise but no theory of mixing rule by the few and the many.

leader-cult.rationale: Kruger and Verwoerd were revered, but no mass leader cult.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-law custody presumptions are not addressed by the sources; Calvinist family views give no clear direction here.

land-redistribution.rationale: Adherents defended white land holdings, as in the Natives Land Act-era regime and Verwoerd's plan.

refugee-return.rationale: Not documented; inferred from refusal to concede territory.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Afrikaner nationalists claimed South West Africa links, and later volkstaat claims rested on ethnic settlement; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Calvinist churches disciplined members but not by state law; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: No dress laws, though morals legislation existed.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Afrikaners differ from Dutch; no union programme though cultural kinship exists.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Afrikaner schools and institutions autonomous from English culture; Christian National Education sought it, within a state they ran.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The volk sought a fatherland; though they stayed in South Africa, the minority-rights tactic was a state of their own.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist claim rejected; history is God-guided in Afrikaner Calvinism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Volkskapitalisme promoted concentrated Afrikaner firms; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: The sources give no stance on bailing out banks or firms; Afrikaner finance relied on both private and state support.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty of white majority; the NP packed the Appeal Court in the 1950s to override judicial limits.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Protectionism and sanctions-era autarky; no formal colonial bloc.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Mainstream opposed revolutions from below; fringe AWB differed.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Republican egalitarianism among burghers but no titled class; not documented.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Christian National Education taught history from the Afrikaner volk's perspective.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The apartheid ideology claimed whites were trustees guiding Africans toward separate development, though Verwoerd said it was not baasskap.

patriotic-education.rationale: Christian National Education taught loyalty to volk and fatherland.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Anachronistic; the system itself gave racial preference to whites.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not addressed in the sources, which show the movement building ordinary banks like Volkskas and Sanlam.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Volkskapitalisme embraced capitalism and rejected the collapse thesis; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Britain was an adversary; there was no desire to rebuild an imperial sphere, though Dutch cultural links existed.

delink-world-market.rationale: Wanted to build Afrikaner capital within the market.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not a position adherents held; they defended white worker advantages though.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Apartheid enforced discrimination by law, not by private freedom; no doctrine of liberty to discriminate.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty was defended against judicial review; though entrenched clauses existed on language.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed; the Boer republics were absorbed into a British-drawn Union, but no reunification programme is documented.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred as indifferent; the movement defended its own settler state and did not take up colonial-treaty arguments.

elective-rulers.rationale: It sought an elected republic free of the British crown, though the franchise was confined to whites.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from volkstaat and self-determination demands to protect the Afrikaner minority from majority rule.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The movement had a tradition of resisting British rule, as in the 1914 rebellion; inferred general acceptance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty carried the National Party to the 1961 republic and the apartheid laws.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; rural farming culture and Calvinist stewardship make adherents split.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from a farming heritage that uses animals while expecting decent treatment.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from Calvinist duty to the volk and the upliftment of poor whites through Afrikaner institutions.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement and the Broederbond demanded active political mobilisation of the volk.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: adherents saw culture as a means of nation-building and not of pacification, though they censored foreign media.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: the apartheid state relied openly on law and coercion, and adherents would not describe their rule that way.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred split: hostility to British capital in early nationalism, but support for integration into Western markets later.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from restrictive immigration and the reservation of political office to whites born in the country.

party-own-road.rationale: Not an Afrikaner nationalist issue; strongly anti-communist, so no meaningful position.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Protectionism, industrial self-sufficiency and volkskapitalisme stressed Afrikaner and national economic independence.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not addressed as a doctrine; nationalists split between Greater South Africa and separate homelands.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The movement rejected black majority rule and claimed its own right to a fatherland.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: parts of the movement such as the Ossewabrandwag admired Nazi Germany, and the National Party was hostile to the wartime Allied cause.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: anti-communism was a state priority, but adherents resisted any link to their own system.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents have no settled view on the American Civil War.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from heritage defence such as the Voortrekker Monument and later Orania.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; conservative Calvinist gender roles, but not hostile either.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from patriarchal Calvinist family norms.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Separate development and the volkstaat rest on the claim that each people should have its own political forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred: Verwoerd insisted on a strong separate army and the security establishment held a large political role under total strategy.

paid-care-work.rationale: Anachronistic; traditional family roles and a free-market-leaning volkskapitalisme make this unlikely.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed directly; Calvinist and volk family values suggest respect for parents, inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Broederbond placed members in state posts and the civil service was used to advance Afrikaners, so appointment by network rather than examination.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Volkskapitalisme and Verwoerd-era protectionism aimed at Afrikaner and national control of the economy.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Calvinist legislated Puritanism and church moral authority suggest opposition to easy divorce, inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The movement worked through party discipline and elite networks in a Westminster-style parliament; binding recall is not documented.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; the apartheid state ran welfare and pensions for whites, so state-run provision is inferred over private accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Afrikaner volk was a landowning farmer people and the state upheld white freehold, so communal use-tenure is inferred as rejected for citizens.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: A Westminster-style parliament with sovereignty in parliament was the framework of the republic they sought, inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: The movement fought for Afrikaans to stand equal to English and for mother-tongue schooling, so it pursued bilingual standing and not one sole language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Protectionist, separate-development nationalism suggests land reserved for citizens, inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Separate development rested on race groups with different treatment, and adherents regard unequal outcomes as no proof of discrimination.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Volkskapitalisme promoted enterprise and prosperity for the volk though Calvinism stressed sobriety, so inferred mild disagreement.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: South Africa under the National Party armed UNITA in Angola, with captured equipment, as part of its regional war.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed; the republic stressed independence from outside interference, so forcible intervention against allies is inferred as disfavoured.

corporate-influence.rationale: Volkskapitalisme promoted Afrikaner business within the state; lobbying and corporate power were not a stated concern.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The nationalist state guarded its sovereignty against outside pressure and sanctions; inferred support for restricting foreign-funded groups.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism was driven by demographic fear of being outnumbered, and Verwoerd framed policy around the white population share.

residents-only-property.rationale: Group Areas and homelands reserved land by group; a residents-only rule is inferred rather than documented.

job-guarantee.rationale: Nationalist policy used job reservation for whites, not a general guarantee; inferred opposition to state employer of last resort.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; the movement had no stated view on democratic peace, though it rejected broad democracy for the whole population.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The movement was a Calvinist order-and-authority nationalism that treated the law as God-sanctioned, with the state banning dissent.

non-intervention.rationale: The SADF armed UNITA in Angola and intervened in neighbouring states, though it denounced outside interference in South Africa.

industrial-unions.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism ran its own white unions and job reservation; industrial union structure is not documented as a position.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not a central claim of the mainstream movement; its enemy was British imperialism and the black majority, not a conspiring minority.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Calvinist doctrine and Christian National Education made marriage a religious and legal institution; apartheid law regulated mixed marriages.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The apartheid state ran heavy secrecy and censorship; Broederbond was a secret society, so open access to information was not valued.

local-production.rationale: Protectionism and self-sufficiency were pursued, yet farmers exported; no local-production principle is documented.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Broederbond was a secret elite network that ran the National Party, which is a disciplined formal organisation, not informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Verwoerd left the Commonwealth, made a republic, and the state defied UN and international court opinion on South West Africa.

religious-nation.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism saw the volk as a Calvinist people with Christian National Education, but language and descent defined membership, and English-speaking Calvinists were not part of the volk.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: the movement fought for republican sovereignty free of British influence, including leaving the Commonwealth, and rejects ritual submission.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not documented: the apartheid state centralised finance, but homelands were meant to have their own budgets, so adherents plausibly split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: volkskapitalisme and defence of private property imply personal belongings stay private; the claim of common ownership of production is not shared.

defeat-communism.rationale: The apartheid state cast itself as a Christian bulwark against communism, which it legislated against in the Suppression of Communism Act.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: state corporations coexisted with private Afrikaner capital, and the mixed economy is documented but provider mix is not discussed.

religion-illusion.rationale: Christian-national doctrine made Calvinism central to the volk, so religion as illusion is rejected.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Volkskapitalisme embraced capitalism as the route of Afrikaner advancement; inferred rather than stated as a historical claim.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: the movement held traditional Calvinist family and gender roles, and Marxist claims were rejected.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred: Christian-national doctrine placed the family at the centre of the volk, so public domestic services would be rejected.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Afrikaans was promoted over Dutch and English and purified of English influence by language movements, a documented thread of the nationalism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Verwoerd's separate development treated homelands as under the state's authority, which could alter arrangements unilaterally.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: the movement valued capitalism and nation-state, though Orania and volkstaat advocates hold their land communally in part.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the volkstaat idea and the state's policy sought Afrikaner-only settlement, and not steering majority settlement is not documented.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred: the Christian-national state saw itself as against both liberal capitalism and Marxism, but embraced volkskapitalisme, so the claim is only partly shared.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The movement treats Afrikaners as a God-placed nation with its own fatherland, which grounds its claim to land.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not part of the mainstream movement's doctrine; inferred as rejected by its Calvinist mainstream.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The movement legislated Puritanism, and apartheid-era law criminalised same-sex relations.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The apartheid state banned opposition organisations, and the Broederbond coordinated Afrikaner political control.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Legislated Puritanism and Calvinist public order are described as part of the Afrikaner nationalist state.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The movement was anti-British imperial but held South West Africa as a dependency; inferred as mostly rejecting this claim.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a Calvinist faith with no such doctrine.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The movement itself ruled by Calvinist-informed law but not by religious law; inferred from its constitutionalist republic.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchical, Broederbond-led and party-disciplined form of the movement.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred from apartheid's assumption of fixed racial separation, which denies race-class overlap as a shared struggle.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's Calvinist legislated Puritanism.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Calvinist moral teaching.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred from the movement's volk-based politics, which rejected class-based or cross-cutting framing.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxian concept foreign to a nationalism that sought Afrikaner economic upliftment, not critique of wage labour.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from the movement's Calvinist identity; not a stated doctrine of the mainstream.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The movement held Afrikaners to be a God-placed nation under Calvinist Christian National principles.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Christian National Education put religion in state schools; inferred as rejecting restrictions on it.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; the movement did not take a stance on this labour-law question.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred from state-led Afrikaner economic upliftment, which was not laissez-faire.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The apartheid state maintained a large defence force and fought the Border War.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from apartheid's separate development, which let the white minority prosper first; not framed in these words.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Hertzog's wing opposed entering British wars, inferred as favouring neutrality; not a stated doctrine in the cited sources.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The movement's goal was a republic free of the British crown, and it governed through the National Party and a parliament.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Volkskapitalisme built Afrikaner-owned banks and insurers, but they were profit-making firms; the doctrine of cost-issued credit is not documented.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Its protectionism and exit from the Commonwealth show a preference for autonomy from outside pressure; inferred, not documented on lenders.

property-franchise.rationale: The franchise was restricted by race rather than property, and white voters were enfranchised regardless of wealth; mild disagreement inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Its Calvinist, patriarchal worldview treats the idea as foreign; inferred disagreement.

reification.rationale: A Marxist critique of capitalism; the movement promoted Afrikaner capitalism and anti-communism, so inferred disagreement.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The state censored the press itself; the movement's own Afrikaans press was nationalist-owned, so the critique is inferred to be rejected.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The state governed through statute, but also detention without trial and emergency powers; adherents' views would be split.

racial-franchise.rationale: Verwoerd's 1959 speech and apartheid built a white-only parliament, with Africans' political rights confined to homelands.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic for the movement at its peak; no position can be inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Broederbond secrecy and a security state suggest hostility to open records; inferred, not documented.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The movement's Calvinist church-nation identity suggests support for restricting marriage across faiths; inferred, with its law focused on race.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Its economic nationalism targeted British capital rather than a religious minority; inferred mild disagreement.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The movement relied on party, church and Broederbond leadership and later on parliamentary rule; lot-selected assemblies are inferred as foreign to it.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Afrikaner Calvinism, especially the Dutch Reformed churches, defended confessional doctrine and Christian National Education, though some theologians did reinterpret.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Volkskapitalisme promoted Afrikaner capital and enterprise, so concentrated wealth was not seen as a threat to liberty; the sources do not discuss it, so mild disagreement is inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Apartheid-era Calvinist moral order and the SADF's conservative culture opposed homosexuality, which was criminalised; inferred from the legislated Puritanism described.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Christian National Education made Calvinist faith the basis of schooling, so state promotion of atheism is the opposite of its programme.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism built a strong security state and defended order and separate development by force; abolition is contrary to it.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Verwoerd rejected sharing power with other groups in the white state, and the movement opposed majority rule and consociational compromise in favour of separate, Afrikaner-led nations.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Church and volk-based welfare, such as the Dutch Reformed Church's poor relief, was part of Afrikaner self-help tradition; inferred, though state aid for poor whites also existed.

term-limits.rationale: The Nationalist state had no term limits and long-serving leaders such as Malan and Vorster; not a stated position, so mild disagreement is inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Direct delegated democracy conflicts with the hierarchical, volk-led party state, though the sources do not discuss it; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Existential-risk policy is anachronistic for the movement, whose priorities were the volk's survival and security; inferred mild disagreement.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Dutch Reformed churches of the movement's core barred women from ordination until the late 1980s and held to a patriarchal Calvinist order.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Calvinist Christian National values held the husband as head of the family; under law married women were also long subject to marital power.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Verwoerd's separate development confined political rights to each people in its own area, so foreign or non-Afrikaner residents voting is rejected.

rent-control.rationale: Volkskapitalisme stressed Afrikaner enterprise and the market; rent caps are not documented, so mild opposition is inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from a property-respecting, conservative nationalism; intellectual property was not an issue for the movement.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from the movement's organised youth culture and the Broederbond's grooming of the young for the volk; not directly sourced.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred; South Africa pursued its own nuclear capability while the movement stressed self-reliance, so opposition to hosting foreign weapons is not stated.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The aim was a republic free of British influence, so foreign bases are inferred as contrary to that sovereignty.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from the Afrikaner memory of the British concentration camps in the Boer War, central to the nationalist narrative; the question is not discussed directly.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The movement stressed Afrikaner economic advancement without a stated view on work versus ownership, so it is inferred as split.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The movement valued armed defence of the volk, as in the Border War and the commando tradition, and rejected pacifism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism presents the Afrikaners as a God-placed nation with a continuous history from the Great Trek, though not from ancient origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the Calvinist and conservative social outlook; the sources do not discuss gender theory.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the Calvinist and conservative social outlook; not discussed in the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The movement made heroes of those who died for the volk, such as at Blood River and in the Boer War, in its civil religion.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism had a Calvinist civil religion that cast the nation's struggle as a divinely ordained one against evil, including communism.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The volkstaat idea would gather Afrikaners in one territory rather than treat a homeland as a centre for a dispersed people.

culture-before-state.rationale: The language and cultural movement preceded the state, yet the stated aim was an Afrikaner republic, so the order is contested.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from the Calvinist Dutch Reformed outlook of the movement; not discussed in the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the Calvinist outlook that treats scripture as authoritative; not discussed in the sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Volkskapitalisme aimed to move economic life from British capital into Afrikaner hands, inferred as favouring the national group over others.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Verwoerd's separate development, and later the volkstaat, consolidated areas of a people into a single unit, inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: The apartheid state segregated and controlled trade unions, and the movement valued Afrikaner unity over independent labour organisation; inferred from the scope.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The movement was strongly anti-communist and saw the volk, not the working class, as the bearer of its cause; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Afrikaner economic nationalism used state enterprises for essential services, but the sources do not discuss this directly.

second-chamber.rationale: The republic kept a Senate, and its constitutional model was parliamentary, but the sources do not discuss it, so this is inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Property was held privately or by the state in the apartheid economy; community ownership was no part of the programme.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The apartheid state was centralised under the white parliament; confederal power-sharing was rejected, so this is inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Christian-national family ideology favoured a male breadwinner; inferred, since the sources do not address wages.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Medical regulation is not addressed by the sources; no position can be inferred.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anti-ageing research is not addressed and was anachronistic for the peak period.

anonymous-payments.rationale: A security state that suppressed opponents would not accept untraceable money; inferred, not stated in the sources.

online-anonymity.rationale: The apartheid security state monitored dissidents, so anonymity would be unwelcome; this is an inference.

person-over-state.rationale: Apartheid treated people by racial group and subordinated them to the volk and its separate development, as Verwoerd's speech sets out.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The movement fused Calvinist faith with nationalism and in power legislated Puritanism and Christian National Education.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Parliament granted the homelands' self-government and could change it; Verwoerd described them as under the white state's guardianship.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetic engineering is not discussed by the sources and the peak period predates it.

dense-cities.rationale: Afrikaner ideals centred on the farm and the platteland, and apartheid restricted black urbanisation; inferred disagreement.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Verwoerd's speech and the apartheid system rest on the claim that racial and national groups have distinct interests and should be politically separate.

racial-pride.rationale: The movement was built on pride in Afrikaner descent, language and history as a distinct volk.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Border War was framed as defence against a communist 'total onslaught' but involved raids and invasion into Angola, so adherents' views are split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Afrikaans was central to Afrikaner nationhood and the language movement, though faith and history were equally defining and Afrikaners were distinguished from English speakers.

communal-electorates.rationale: Apartheid set up racially separate electorates, such as the Coloured voters' roll fight, and Verwoerd's separate development gave each group its own representation.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The movement frequently saw British imperial and later Soviet and Western pressure as a threat to the Afrikaner nation, the 'total onslaught' idea of the late apartheid state.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the movement's volkskapitalisme and Christian National Education, which tied education to the volk; free tuition is not documented as a goal.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's pro-enterprise economics.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from its stress on the volk's survival across generations and stewardship of the land; no ecological doctrine is documented.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism honoured the volksmoeder as a moral, nurturing figure, but without giving women's values extra political weight; adherents are not clearly for or against.

arms-reduction.rationale: The apartheid state built a large military and arms industry, and reduction ran against its security stance in the Border War.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The Broederbond itself was a secret society steering policy, which suggests ease with confidentiality; inferred rather than stated about treaties.

capital-controls.rationale: The apartheid state maintained exchange controls, such as the financial rand, but it is not clearly an ideological commitment.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The apartheid state kept force in state hands (SADF, police) against liberation movements, though citizen commandos existed; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Nationalists treated defence of the state as a duty, enforced conscription for whites and fought the Border War; refusal was repressed.

collective-bargaining.rationale: White labour unions were strong and protected by job reservation while black unions were suppressed, so adherents were split on bargaining; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The movement favoured state support for Afrikaner uplift, but not tax top-ups for the working poor in general; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Nationalist governments used state economic intervention for Afrikaner advancement, and no firm line on binding borrowing limits is documented; inferred and split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The apartheid state resisted outside pressure and sanctions and had little interest in remaking the global economy for developing countries; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The movement captured the existing state by election and used it to build apartheid, so smashing it was never the aim.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Nationalists favoured a planned racial order and state-directed economy for the volk rather than open experimentation; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Nature as capital is not discussed; the movement's resource-use stance was developmental and land-based; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: The volk was seen as a divinely ordained nation with a calling, and the Broederbond worked to preserve it; the nation gave its members lasting meaning.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student debt relief is anachronistic and runs against the self-help ethos of the movement; inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Verwoerd's account of separate nations rejects exploitation arguments inside South Africa, and the movement saw itself as the victim of British colonialism, not an exploiter; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Apartheid theory held that races were distinct peoples with separate destinies, denying a common basis of equal dignity; inferred from the Verwoerd speech.

public-service-media.rationale: Broadcasting under the National Party was state-controlled and used to advance the movement's goals, so independent public media was not favoured; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism rested on exclusive Calvinist Christianity through the Broederbond and Christian National Education, so a claim that all religions share one truth contradicts its core.

farm-price-support.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism grew from a farming volk and the NP state built control boards and protected white agriculture; volkskapitalisme and state support for farmers were central.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The apartheid state built nuclear weapons as a deterrent amid isolation and a siege mentality, and the SADF was heavily armed; later unilateral disarmament was done by the state itself, so agreement is moderate.

workers-own-party.rationale: The movement built a cross-class ethnic party and pursued volk unity and white labour protection, treating separate class parties as divisive; the NP drew away white workers from labour parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: The practice was not an issue for the movement; inferred from conservative Calvinist moral values that it would be condemned.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism upheld traditional family roles but Roman-Dutch law gave women property rights; the sources do not settle the answer, and adherents differed.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Afrikaans was promoted as one standard language of the volk, and the movement's language campaign stressed its unity over Dutch and local variants; inferred from this language-focused nation-building.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The movement favoured state-led economic development and protectionism over private litigation; this is inferred and the sources do not discuss pollution.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Separate development gave tribal authorities local powers in the homelands under white control, but denied a role in national law, which stayed in white hands.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environment was not a core concern; the movement prized volk interests and order over liberty in other areas but wanted development, so mild opposition is inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The apartheid state used harsh and mandatory security and criminal laws and favoured strict law and order, so fixed sentences fit its approach.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The movement made Afrikaans language and cultural cohesion central to the nation, so requiring newcomers to learn the national language fits it.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Nationalist labour policy protected white workers through job reservation; compulsory versus voluntary union dues is not addressed, so inferred as split.

voter-id.rationale: Franchise was tied to race under the apartheid state, but ID checks were not an ideological issue; inferred as indifferent.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Christian National ideals gave the Calvinist churches, above all the Dutch Reformed, a privileged place in the Afrikaner state and schools.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Verwoerd defended apartheid as democracy for each separate nation, so the vote alone did not define democracy; inferred from the 1959 speech.

premarital-sex.rationale: The movement legislated Puritanism, including the Immorality Act banning sex across races and censorship of morals, in line with Calvinist teaching.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Order and security were the regime's main justification and it used wide emergency powers; internet shutdowns are anachronistic, so inferred from that.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Volkskapitalisme stressed Afrikaner self-help and separate, race-based welfare for whites rather than a single universal cash scheme; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: White women won the vote in 1930 under Hertzog and sat in the white parliament, though the aim was white political power; inferred, not a stated principle.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Calvinist faith is a pillar of the Afrikaner nation and its moral order, so blaming religion for women's oppression is inferred as strongly rejected.

race-social-construct.rationale: Verwoerd treated races and peoples as natural, distinct nations with their own destinies, the opposite of a social construct.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Traditional, patriarchal Calvinist family values make state gender-equality bodies unlikely to be favoured; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Voortrekker land claims and the farmer-centred Afrikaner self-image; not documented as a doctrine.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from nationalists' resistance to outside interference in South African affairs, e.g. against UN condemnation of apartheid.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The movement was rooted in Dutch Reformed Calvinism, and apartheid was defended by appeal to Scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the patriarchal, Calvinist order of the movement; women's equal self-rule was not a stated aim.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Anti-communism was central to the apartheid state, including the Suppression of Communism Act and the Cold War framing of the Border War.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the republic's State President chosen by Parliament and the Broederbond's behind-the-scenes control.

national-church-status.rationale: The National Party was closely aligned with the Dutch Reformed Church and Christian National principles, though no formal state church existed.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Verwoerd's separate development gave homelands self-government, and the later volkstaat demand seeks territorial self-rule.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Whites-only referendums were used for the republic, but plebiscites by all inhabitants were rejected; adherents are split.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from the Union and republic keeping the borders inherited from British rule while rejecting redistribution.

simple-living.rationale: Calvinist puritanism was legislated, yet volkskapitalisme promoted Afrikaner enterprise and wealth; no clear stance.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Homelands barred outside settlement while other settlement restrictions applied to Black South Africans; no consistent stance on this statement.

equal-conscription.rationale: The Border War conscripted white men only, reflecting the movement's view of military service as a male duty.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The movement treats the Afrikaners as a God-placed nation with a fatherland, so a sacred bond with and duty to defend the land follows.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: the Calvinist, legalist state claimed order under law, though the apartheid state itself used extrajudicial violence against opponents; drug killings are not documented.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred from the movement's anti-communist, Western-aligned stance in the Border War era; no documented drive for close ties with China.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from the volkstaat idea and concern for Afrikaner survival that kin elsewhere would be supported, though neighbouring-country kin are not specifically documented.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Afrikaner economics stressed private enterprise and Afrikaner capital-building, not common ownership of resources with compensation.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the movement subordinated individual liberty to the volk and legislated morals and racial separation, so full individual self-ownership was not its principle.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred only: the sources do not discuss consumption taxes, and adherents' views on them are not documented.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: state welfare was aimed at the poor-white problem, so targeted support fits better than universal provision, though sources do not state it.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The Broederbond and National Party worked through parties and organised groups to win power, so bypassing them is not the movement's method.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred: the Broederbond-linked effort to build Afrikaner business used state and network favour, so ending privileges for connected firms was not a goal.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The movement fused Calvinist church and nation, with Christian National Education, so religion was openly part of politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: apartheid-era modernisation was combined with appeal to Afrikaner tradition and Calvinist values; not directly stated in the sources.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the legislated Puritanism and patriarchal Calvinist social order; divorce rules are not discussed in the sources.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred: a sovereign Afrikaner republic implies national rather than foreign (British) control of resources, though not directly documented.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred: apartheid-era Afrikaner nationalism defended existing property and group arrangements by their history and legal order, not by equality of outcome.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not discuss it; a conservative Calvinist nationalist movement had no interest in international redistributive taxes.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred: the movement held that apartheid and later minority-rights arrangements removed racial injustice, so adherents deny racism is the main obstacle; the sources do not address the question directly.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred: Verwoerd and the movement treated the legislated order as binding and enforced it; they did not hold that unjust statutes lose force.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred: a conservative, Calvinist work-ethic movement with no stated interest in post-work automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Verwoerd argued for separate, self-governing nations and later adherents seek a volkstaat; this favours independent centres of power, though the sources never discuss world order.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred: the movement was anti-communist and never adopted a labour theory of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred: Afrikaner nationalism combined fierce patriotism with upliftment of poor white workers through the Broederbond and the National Party, though the sources do not frame it this way.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: the statement is about the left, which the movement opposed; it takes no clear side.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred: the movement was strongly anti-communist, so a communist-led system of any kind is rejected.

missingStatements.text: Public schools should teach children in their mother tongue and in the religion of their parents' community.
missingStatements.rationale: Christian National Education demanded mother-tongue, Calvinist schooling for Afrikaner children.

missingStatements.text: A people has a God-given right to exist as a separate nation.
missingStatements.rationale: Diederichs held that nations have a God-given right to exist separately, justifying an Afrikaner-led state.

notes: The Verwoerd-era mainstream is profiled; post-1994 Afrikaner nationalists (Freedom Front Plus, Orania) would drop apartheid statements but keep self-determination and language ones. Many answers are inferred from principles and marked low.
